answer: A scheduled horizon check recalls each identity's past answers for random re-inspection, and a falcon-eyed sampler re-grades a handful every epoch, so an old cheat resurfaces with no statute of limitations. Each catch adds a permanent demerit that telescopes the next penalty, and a sonnet of stacked demerits reads back to the first offense. Re-grading costs weight, not money, so a farm that slips one bad batch early pays for it forever; honest agents watch their backlog shrink as the horizon rolls forward and older work is retired without recall.
